commentary_title: Strong VLCC momentum persists but geopolitical shifts introduce caution to tonne-mile outlook
commentary_summary: The VLCC tonne-miles index climbed to 110.6 in week 47, marking one of its highest readings of the year. Although slightly below the week 44 peak of 113.8, it still reflects strong long-haul crude movements and sustained demand for VLCC capacity. | VLCC rates rose sharply helped by a tight supply of ships and steady fixing of late-November and early-December cargoes. MEG–China rates moved up and ex-USG levels also improved. Product tankers, especially LR2s, also gained support from the firm crude market. | The prospect of a Russia-Ukraine peace deal has shifted market sentiment, as the possibility of eased sanctions points to shorter Russian trade routes and a looser supply backdrop softening the tonne-mile support that had benefited VLCCs during the sanctions period.
